extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent examiners, patent applicants/representatives, and public stakeholders interested in USPTO performance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and performance standards describing how the USPTO measures, validates, and seeks to improve patent quality and timeliness, including specific metrics (pendency, cost per production unit), data verification practices, pilots/programs to improve clarity and correctness, and international work-sharing initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability for performance data
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility for providing performance data lies with managers of USPTO programs who are held accountable for making certain that procedures are in place to ensure the accuracy of data and that performance measurement sources are complete and reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must ensure procedures exist to guarantee data accuracy and completeness. OCFO monitors agency performance and provides direction/support on data-collection methodology and analysis. Accountability is an explicit responsibility assigned to program management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality control of automated systems and databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated systems and databases that collect, track, and store performance indicators are monitored and maintained by USPTO program managers, with systems support provided by OCIO. Each system incorporates internal program edits to control the accuracy of supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edits should evaluate data for reasonableness, consistency, and accuracy. Crosschecks between internal systems provide additional assurance. External experts routinely review data-collection methodology. Examples of systems: Patent Application Location and Monitoring, Trademark Reporting and Application Monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data accuracy, verification, and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO conducts verification and validation of performance measures periodically to ensure quality, reliability, and credibility. Sampling techniques and sample counts are reviewed and adjusted to ensure statistical reliability for inferences about the population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the start of each fiscal year and at points during reporting periods, sampling and analyses are adjusted; analyses identify statistically significant trends and factors affecting indicators. For examination quality, review programs assess reviewer variability, data-entry errors, and biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of patent quality (correctness and clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality patents are patents that are correctly issued in compliance with all the requirement of Title 35 as well as the relevant case law at the time of issuance, and that provide clarity in the prosecution record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality comprises both correctness (legal compliance) and clarity (clear reasoning and record). USPTO initiatives (EPQI, Master Review Form, training) emphasize clarity of examiner reasoning while maintaining focus on correctness. Clear prosecution records reduce litigation and provide market certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master Review Form standardization
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize reviews of finished work products, such as USPTO office actions, through use of a single Master Review Form that places much greater emphasis on assessing the clarity of an examiner’s reasoning while maintaining focus on correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form uses smart form logic so reviewers see only applicable sections/questions. It captures both correctness and clarity via standardized questions and is the foundation for revised quality metrics and targeted training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Metrics Program (new patent quality metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop new patent quality metrics (to replace the Quality Composite Score) using existing data (e.g., QIR) and new data (e.g., Master Review Form data) to create world-class, revised quality measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics development is informed by stakeholder feedback via Federal Register comments and workshops; proposed metrics aim to better reflect quality and will be iteratively developed and revised. Because metrics may change, historical trend portrayal may be limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and Correctness Data Capture Program
rubrics_metrics.description: A system enabling reviewers in the Office of Patent Quality Assurance and the Technology Centers to consistently document and access office action quality review data, including the Master Review Form to capture clarity and correctness information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to provide consistent documentation and retrieval of review data to support measurement, analysis, and training; built using feedback from Federal Register comments and public workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of the Record Pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify best practices for enhancing clarity of specific aspects of the prosecution record—claim interpretation, reasons for allowance, and interview summaries—and explore the impact of implementing these best practices during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot seeks to create a complete, comprehensive record to give inventors and investors confidence and to avoid costly litigation. Findings may inform examiner guidance and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent timeliness (pendency) measures and targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent timeliness is measured primarily by Average First Action Pendency (time from filing to initial determination) and Average Total Pendency (time from filing to issue or abandonment). The USPTO set targets of 10 months for first action pendency and 20 months for total pendency (FY2019 targets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency results are tracked annually and by technology center; fluctuations reflect filing volumes and workload. USPTO monitors incoming filings and adjusts long-term planning to meet targets. Patents Dashboard provides transparency on these measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Average First Action Pendency metric
rubrics_metrics.description: First action pendency measures the time from when an application is filed until it receives an initial determination of patentability by the patent examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to gauge examination responsiveness; reported annually (tables provided). Efforts to reduce first action pendency include workforce management, initiatives like Track One, and process improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Average Total Pendency metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Total pendency measures the time from filing until an application is either issued as a patent or abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects end-to-end system performance; measured and reported annually. Reduction efforts include backlog reduction and programs affecting prosecution efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total Cost Per Patent Production Unit (efficiency metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative measure of efficiency: calculated by taking the total cost of the Patent process for the fiscal year (including support costs) and dividing by the total number of Patent Production Units (PUs) for the same period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PUs are an internal measure of work completed (including design and PCT PUs). The measure is not a true 'total cost' because activities contributing to a PU may span multiple years; use for relative trend/efficiency analysis rather than absolute accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Grant Outcomes Program objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide examiners access to post-grant information (e.g., content of AIA trial proceedings and their prior art) to (1) enhance patentability determinations in related child applications, (2) target examiner training, and (3) provide examiner education via periodic reviews of post grant outcomes focusing on technology sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program improves examiner searches and examination quality by notifying examiners of related patents undergoing AIA trials and streamlining access to AIA trial contents; used to gather best practices and to inform training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Prosecution Pilot (P3) — after-final panel review
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows an applicant with a utility patent application to submit a proposed after-final amendment for consideration by a panel of experienced examiners, present oral arguments to the panel (in-person or by phone), and receive a brief written summary of the status of pending claims and reasoning for maintaining any rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P3 combines popular aspects of AFCP 2.0 and Pre-Appeal Pilot; it provides a new path for after-final amendments and detailed panel explanations to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant assistance and prioritized processing programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs designed to advance patent prosecution and assist applicants include Track One (prioritized examination), First Action Interview, Quick Path Information Disclosure Statement (QPIDS), After Final Consideration Program 2.0 (AFCP 2.0), and new pilots like P3 and Post Grant Outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These initiatives are intended to streamline prosecution, provide earlier examiner-applicant engagement, accelerate review for certain matters (e.g., Patents 4 Patients), and reduce cycle times. Applicants may opt into some programs subject to eligibility and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents Dashboard transparency and analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: An online Patents Dashboard provides public access to USPTO progress metrics (pendency, quality, timeliness) and has been expanded to include technology center-level statistics and frequent quarterly updates addressing topics of interest to the patent community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dashboard improvements respond to public feedback and aim to make contributing factors to examination delays more visible, enabling better planning and targeted improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationwide Workforce Program (workforce model to improve capacity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a nationwide workforce by utilizing regional offices, telework, and other measures to hire and retain skilled IP professionals who may not relocate to DC; this model aims to enhance examiner retention and decrease the number of patent applications waiting for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program expands the candidate pool, reduces real estate costs, and improves national presence/outreach. Regional offices operate with regional directors, outreach staff, examiners, management, admin, and IT staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: International cooperation and work sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in work sharing and collaboration with international IP offices (Global PPH, bilateral PPH agreements, Collaborative Search Pilots with JPO and KIPO, IP5 PCT Collaborative Search pilot) and enable electronic sharing of dossier information (Global Dossier) to improve efficiency and examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing search and examination results can accelerate examination and reduce duplication. USPTO revised procedures to facilitate electronic exchange of information unless applicant opts out. CPC cooperation and agreements (e.g., Israel classifying into CPC) further enhance global searchability and harmonization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic Submission for Case Studies Program
rubrics_metrics.description: A public program allowing stakeholders to suggest topics for case studies to be conducted by the Office of Patent Quality Assurance; six case studies were selected for ongoing review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a mechanism for public input into quality investigations; case studies inform broader quality-improvement activities and policy.
